slides.content: Administrative principle, Geographic location, Agricultural land use, Marketing principle, Least cost, Possibilism, Development, Service centers, Economic growth, Settlements, Geographic determinism, Transportation principle.

slides.title: 5.2 Climate Extremes and Poverty
slides.content: Extreme events (droughts, floods) worsen poverty. Poor people more vulnerable. 'Poverty traps' occur when repeated shocks erode livelihoods. SSA and South Asia most vulnerable.

slides.title: 5.2 Key Terms
slides.content: Climate extremes, Critical thresholds, Droughts, Flooding events, Impacts, Poverty traps, Vulnerability.

slides.title: 5.3 Disadvantages of Landlocked Countries
slides.content: No direct sea access. Higher transport costs, dependence on transit neighbors, political vulnerability. Examples: Ethiopia, which relies on Djibouti, Sudan.

slides.title: 5.3 Key Terms
slides.content: Disadvantages, Landlocked countries, Sea access, Political disadvantages, Transportation disadvantages.

slides.title: 5.4 Intraregional Trade in Africa
slides.content: Increased intra-African trade but still low. SADC and COMESA dominate. South Africa largest exporter. Barriers: tariffs, non-tariff measures, administrative delays.

slides.title: 5.4 Key Terms
slides.content: Intra-Regional trade, Commodity, Exports, Imports, Trade flows, Trade policies, Trade challenges.

slides.title: Unit 6: Major Global Environmental Changes
slides.content: Persistent Environmental Changes, Poverty-Environment Nexus, Environmental Degradation and Sustainable Development.

slides.title: 6.1 Persistent Environmental Changes
slides.content: Habitat destruction, Agricultural intensification (impacts on biodiversity, soil), Overexploitation (fishing, logging, water), Invasive species (terrestrial, aquatic).

slides.title: 6.1 Key Terms
slides.content: Agricultural intensification, Overexploitation of resources, Environmental changes, Habitat destruction, Invasive alien species.

slides.title: 6.2 Poverty-Environment Nexus
slides.content: The 'vicious cycle': poverty leads to degradation (land, deforestation) which worsens poverty. Integrated approaches needed to address both.

slides.title: 6.2 Key Terms
slides.content: Deforestation, Environment, Land degradation, Poverty.

slides.title: 6.3 Environmental Degradation and Sustainable Development
slides.content: Types: soil, water, atmospheric degradation. Causes: land disturbance, pollution, overpopulation. Effects: health, biodiversity loss, resource scarcity. Sustainable development: meeting present needs without compromising future generations.

slides.title: 6.3 Key Terms
slides.content: Environmental degradation, Sustainable development.

slides.title: Unit 7: Geographic Issues and Public Concerns
slides.content: Population-related concerns, Land degradation & desertification, Drought & famine, Deforestation, Digital Divide.

slides.title: 7.1 Population-Related Concerns
slides.content: Challenges in DCs: rapid growth, urbanization. Family size, education, income interconnections. Malthusian vs. Anti-Malthusian views. Unemployment and underemployment issues.

slides.title: 7.1 Key Terms
slides.content: Economic growth rates, Household income, Education, Population growth, Employment, Underemployment, Unemployment, Family size, Household, Economic Dependency Ratio (EDR).

slides.title: 7.2 Land Degradation and Desertification
slides.content: Long-term loss of land quality. Forms: physical, chemical, biological. Causes: natural and human. Desertification: degradation in drylands. Impacts: reduced productivity, biodiversity loss. Mitigation: terracing, water harvesting.

slides.title: 7.2 Key Terms
slides.content: Desertification, Land degradation, Physical degradation, Chemical degradation, Biological degradation.

slides.title: 7.3 Recurrent Droughts and Famines
slides.content: Drought: prolonged moisture deficiency (meteorological, hydrological, agricultural, socioeconomic). Famine: severe food shortage. Link between drought and famine. Impacts: crop failure, food insecurity. Mitigation: early warning, water management.

slides.title: 7.3 Key Terms
slides.content: Drought, Famine.

slides.title: 7.4 Deforestation
slides.content: Removal of forests. Underlying causes: population pressure, policy. Proximate causes: clearing for farms, logging. Consequences: biodiversity loss, climate change, soil erosion. Solutions: afforestation, reforestation, alternative energy.

slides.title: 7.4 Key Terms
slides.content: Deforestation.

slides.title: 7.5 The Digital Divide
slides.content: Gap in ICT access. Driven by income, education, location. Consequences: loss of jobs, inequality. Advantages of digitalization: access to education, telemedicine.

slides.title: 7.5 Key Terms
slides.content: Digital divide.

slides.title: Unit 8: Geo-Spatial Information and Data Processing
slides.content: Representation of Relief on Topographic Maps, Basic GIS Concepts, ArcMap and Main Tools.

slides.title: 8.1 Representation of Relief Features
slides.content: Relief: difference in elevation. Hachures: show slope direction. Contours: lines of equal elevation. Properties: never cross, never branch. Representing landforms: hills (concentric), valleys (V-shape), depressions (tick marks), etc.

slides.title: 8.1 Key Terms
slides.content: Contour, Hachures, Relief features, Topographic map.

slides.title: 8.2 Basic Concepts of GIS
slides.content: Computer-based system for spatial data. Components: Hardware, Software, Data, People, Methods. Data types: Vector (points, lines, polygons) and Raster (grids). Spatial data (location) vs. Attribute data (characteristics).

slides.title: 8.2 Key Terms
slides.content: GIS, Spatial data, Attribute data, Vector data, Raster data.

slides.title: 8.3 ArcMap and Main Tools
slides.content: Opening, saving, closing documents (.mxd). Main menus and tools (Add Data, Zoom, Identify, Measure). ArcToolbox (analysis, conversion tools). Adding, removing, displaying data. Data View vs. Layout View.

slides.title: 8.3 Key Terms
slides.content: Adding, ArcMap, Closing, Displaying, Opening, Removing, Saving, Tools.
